caption: Performance of different triggers. The words used as triggers on the horizontal axis are arranged in ascending order according to the ASR of the clean model.
model_annotation: The line plot illustrates the performance of different trigger words in terms of their attack success rate (ASR) under a clean-label poisoning scenario, where the poison rate is 5% (2.6% of the total dataset). The horizontal axis displays various trigger words—such as "bb," "mb," "cf," "beautiful," "excellent," "gorgeous," "wonderful," "brilliant," "stunning," and "beautifully"—arranged in ascending order based on the ASR of the clean model. The vertical axis represents the ASR, ranging from 0.2 to 0.9. Three distinct lines are plotted: the green line with circle markers, labeled "start," shows a generally increasing trend with some fluctuations, starting at approximately 0.2 and ending near 0.9. The orange line with cross markers, labeled "random," exhibits a more erratic pattern, starting at around 0.5, dropping sharply to 0.2 at "cf," then rising to about 0.9 at "beautifully." The purple line with circle markers, labeled "end," follows a fluctuating path, beginning at approximately 0.5, peaking near 0.9 at "wonderful," and ending around 0.85. The legend in the lower right corner identifies the three lines corresponding to different trigger types.
